final.risk: Structural inflation and higher-for-longer term premiums on long-duration sovereign debt, exacerbated by increased Treasury supply [D03].
final.market_implied_probability: Implied by the rise in 30-year yields to 4.17% [D02] and recent fiscal downgrade [D03].
final.our_probability_and_why: Moderate-to-high. While disinflation is occurring, the scale of Treasury issuance and the risk of structural inflation suggest that the bond market has not fully priced the long-term term premium [D01], [D03].
final.instrument: Payer swaptions on long-term interest rates [D04].
final.exit_rule: Exit when the asymmetry is resolved, either through realized rate increases hitting our target or a meaningful shift in the fiscal/inflation paradigm that removes the tail-risk protection requirement [D06].

drivers.driver: Persistently elevated core inflation requires a term-premium risk adjustment not yet fully reflected in long-bond yields.
Increased Treasury net marketable borrowing supply creates technical pressure on long-duration yields.
Existing option protection provides essential tail-risk coverage for our concentrated equity positions at an established cost.

final.memo:
Our portfolio remains concentrated in high-quality, free-cash-flow-generative businesses that are generally durable, but we remain mindful of the sensitivity of long-duration assets to discount rate volatility [D05]. The current macro environment exhibits a tug-of-war between observed disinflation and the structural risks of significant fiscal deficits and increased Treasury issuance [D01], [D03].

Given that we have already deployed capital into long-rate payer swaptions to protect against the paradigm-shifting risk of inflation and term-premium expansion, we view this as a decision to maintain our hedge [D04], [D05]. We do not believe the market has adequately compensated for the fiscal outlook or the potential for long-term yields to remain higher than historical averages [D02]. We continue to hold our existing protection to ensure our portfolio is resilient against a sharp, disorderly move in the long end of the curve, rather than attempting to trade the interim noise [D06].
